Let j = r-k, then j runs from 0 to 2014 - k, so inner sum = \sum_{j=0}^{2014 - k} \binom{2019}{ j }.

Thus S = \sum_{k=0}^{2014} (-1)^k (k+1)(k+2) A_{2014 - k}, where A_m = \sum_{j=0}^m \binom{2019}{ j }.

We have partial sums of binomial coefficients. This is reminiscent of using identity: \sum_{j=0}^m \binom{n}{j} = 2^{n-1} + \frac{1}{2} \binom{n}{ \lfloor n/2 \rfloor } ... not a simple closed form. But maybe the sum telescopes if we use generating functions.

Thus S = \sum_{r=0}^{2014} c_r where c_r = (a*b)_r.

\]

---

### 1.  View the inner sum as a convolution  

Define  

\[
a_k=(-1)^k(k+1)(k+2)\qquad (k\ge0),\qquad 
b_j=\binom{2019}{j}\qquad(0\le j\le2019).
\]

For a fixed \(r\)

\[
c_r=\sum_{k=0}^{r}a_k\,b_{r-k}
\]

is the convolution \((a*b)_r\).  
Hence  

\[
S=\sum_{r=0}^{2014}c_r .
\]

If we let  

\[
A(x)=\sum_{k\ge0}a_kx^k ,\qquad 
B(x)=\sum_{j=0}^{2019}b_jx^j ,
\]

then  

\[
C(x)=A(x)B(x)=\sum_{r\ge0}c_rx^r .
\]

---

### 2.  Compute the generating functions  

\[
\begin{aligned}
A(x)&=\sum_{k\ge0}(-1)^k(k+1)(k+2)x^{k}
      =\sum_{k\ge0}(k+1)(k+2)(-x)^{k}\\[2mm]
    &=\frac{2}{(1+ x)^{3}}\qquad\text{(since }\sum_{k\ge0}(k+1)(k+2)x^{k}= \frac{2}{(1-x)^{3}}\text{)} .
\end{aligned}
\]

\[
B(x)=\sum_{j=0}^{2019}\binom{2019}{j}x^{j}=(1+x)^{2019}.
\]

Therefore  

\[
C(x)=A(x)B(x)=\frac{2}{(1+x)^{3}}(1+x)^{2019}=2(1+x)^{2016}.
\]

---

### 3.  Extract the coefficients  

From \(C(x)=2(1+x)^{2016}\),

\[
c_r=2\binom{2016}{r}\qquad (0\le r\le2016),
\]
and \(c_r=0\) for \(r>2016\).

---

### 4.  Sum the required coefficients  

\[
\begin{aligned}
S&=\sum_{r=0}^{2014}c_r
   =2\sum_{r=0}^{2014}\binom{2016}{r}\\
  &=2\Biggl(\sum_{r=0}^{2016}\binom{2016}{r}
            -\binom{2016}{2015}
            -\binom{2016}{2016}\Biggr)\\
  &=2\Bigl(2^{2016}-2016-1\Bigr)\\
  &=2^{2017}-4034 .
\end{aligned}
\]
